public_rationale: The forecast is conditional. The reviewed evidence does not establish a broad AI bubble collapse, so its predicted aftermath cannot yet be scored. Funding difficulties alone do not establish the trigger, and continued AI investment does not refute what might happen after a future collapse.
limitations: The trigger has no numerical definition.
The cited venture-market summary cannot establish conditions throughout the entire technology industry.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If the AI bubble pops, the entire tech industry will suffer and venture capitalists will be washed out.

statement.excerpt: If the AI bubble pops, the entire tech industry will suffer as venture capitalists are once again washed out through chasing an unprofitable, barely-substantiated trend.

from_speaker: the entire tech industry will suffer
venture capitalists are once again washed out
our_interpretation: A bubble popping means a broad, sustained collapse in AI investment or valuations, rather than an isolated company failure or brief market selloff.
Industry-wide suffering means substantial harm across the technology sector; venture capitalists being washed out means severe investment losses and impaired fundraising.
The claim concerns sector-wide effects, not a specified company's financial metric.
The collapse must cause the predicted harm.
criteria.support_condition: An established AI investment collapse followed by broad technology-sector harm and severe venture-capital losses attributable to that collapse.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An established collapse followed by a sufficiently documented aftermath in which the technology sector and venture investors broadly avoid the predicted harm.
